messages:
clare: Quick heads-up  i'm opening a tiny PR to add a short "Bench reporting & variant mapping" section to the model-card template. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1702 :wave:

omar: Good. Make the required fields explicit: device, seq_len, batch, warmup_iters, quant_variant, seq_limit, p50/p95, tokens_per_s, and whether numbers are lab vs hosted.

jen: Add a 2-row illustrative example showing fp16 vs int8 deltas and a one-line balance for normalization. Keep it compact so writers don't paste full matrices.

clare: Plan: add a short YAML example block in the template, one copyable perf-harness command, and a brief GFLOP-normalized formula marked as heuristic. Example YAML I'll include: 
```
tested_devices: [a100,h100]
variants:
  - name: polaris13b-fp16
    seq_limit: 8192
    notes: "lab: a100, seq=1024, batch=1"
  - name: polaris13b-int8
    seq_limit: 4096
    notes: "lab: a100-int8, seq=1024, batch=1; lower seq ceiling"
benchmark_notes: "warmup=50 iters=400; tokens_per_s steady-state
"
```

omar: For perf-harness snippet, include exact flags so it's copy/paste: 
```
python perf_harness.py --model polaris13b --seq_len 1024 --batch 1 --iters 400 --device a100 --quant fp16 --collect p50,p95,tokens_per_s
```

jen: And a worked normalization example: norm_tps = measured_tps * (device_gflops / baseline_gflops) with a short: "heuristic only; use lab runs for canonical numbers."

clare: I'll also scan for stale perf links and replace /perf/benchmarks with https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness#readme and list changed files in the PR description.

omar: Reviewer plan: eng-ml for numbers + normalization sanity-check, eng-runtime for variant field names, docs for editorial. If canonical numbers change, create a perf follow-up GH issue and add CHANGENOTES.

docs-bot: I will post the standard PR checklist and add labels on open (docs, perf-needed if numbers changed). (automated)

clare: One tiny UX ask  add a one-line reminder at the top of the template: "Include baseline machine + test conditions (seq_len, batch, warmup)" so it isn't omitted. Drafting now; ETA today. last_message_ts=3765432234
